title: Commerce
name: Commerce
metaDescription: Commerce 1031 exchange advisory for owners of rail-served industrial buildings near the I-5/I-710 interchange and Citadel Outlets-area retail parcels.

sections.html: Commerce is a small city built almost entirely around industrial and distribution use, with rail lines and freeway access doing more to define its real estate than population ever will. An owner selling in Commerce is typically holding a warehouse or distribution building on a rail-served parcel, and the replacement search that follows needs to weigh rail access and freeway proximity as heavily as square footage.

sections.heading: Why Rail Access Still Drives Commerce Industrial Value
sections.html:
Commerce sits along Union Pacific and BNSF lines that connect the Alameda Corridor rail network to inland distribution points, and buildings with active rail spurs carry a premium over comparable dock-high warehouses without one, since a tenant that ships by rail has few other cities in the county to choose from. That premium holds even when the building itself is older, because replicating a rail spur on a new parcel elsewhere in the county is rarely possible given how built out the surrounding land already is.

The city's freeway position, close to where Interstate 5 and Interstate 710 come together, adds a second layer of demand from trucking and last-mile distribution tenants who need both rail-adjacent and freeway-adjacent options within the same building search.

sections.heading: The Categories an Owner Actually Compares in Commerce
sections.html:
Because the city is so heavily industrial, a Commerce identification list tends to stay narrow, drawing from:

  • Rail-served warehouse and distribution buildings
  • Dock-high logistics buildings near the I-5/I-710 interchange
  • Outlet and destination retail parcels near the Citadel corridor
  • Small owner-user manufacturing buildings on legacy industrial lots
  • DST interests for owners exiting active industrial management

sections.heading: Lender and Environmental Considerations on Older Commerce Parcels
sections.html:
Lenders generally underwrite Commerce industrial favorably given the scarcity of comparable rail-served land, but a buyer should still order a Phase I environmental review on older buildings, since decades of industrial and manufacturing use across the city means prior tenants can leave soil or groundwater conditions that are not obvious from a walk-through. That review should be ordered the same week a property is identified, not after financing is already underway.

Retail near the Citadel Outlets corridor underwrites differently than the surrounding industrial stock, and a buyer moving from a warehouse into that kind of destination retail should expect the lender to focus more on tenant sales performance and less on the physical building than an industrial loan would.

sections.heading: Building an Identification List Around a Narrow Market
sections.html: Because Commerce is almost entirely built out, an owner exiting one rail-served building and hoping to identify another inside the same city may need to widen the search to nearby industrial submarkets to have enough comparable options by the forty-five day deadline. The 200 percent rule tends to fit better here than the three-property rule once the search crosses into neighboring cities, since rail-served and non-rail industrial buildings do not behave as close substitutes for underwriting purposes.

sections.heading: Budgeting a Commerce Industrial Purchase Beyond Purchase Price
sections.html:
A numbers-first budget for a Commerce replacement should carry the Phase I environmental review as a hard line item rather than a contingency, given the depth of industrial history across the city, along with a separate reserve for rail-spur maintenance if the building carries an active connection, since that infrastructure is the tenant's responsibility in some leases and the landlord's in others. Confirming which side of that split applies before closing avoids an unbudgeted repair bill in year one.

Lifecycle cost on older Commerce warehouse buildings also deserves a hard look at roof condition and dock-door equipment, since decades-old tilt-up construction common in this pocket of the county often needs roof replacement sooner than a buyer coming from a newer submarket would expect. Pricing that into the offer, rather than treating an occupied building as maintenance-free, keeps the post-closing budget realistic and protects the return an investor modeled going into the exchange. An owner should request roof and dock-equipment inspection reports from the seller before finalizing price, since those two systems drive most of the unbudgeted capital spending on Commerce industrial buildings in the years right after closing. A buyer comparing several Commerce candidates should build a simple cost-per-square-foot model that separates purchase price from expected near-term capital spend, since two buildings priced identically on paper can carry very different total costs once roof and dock condition are factored in.

faqs.q: Why do rail-served buildings in Commerce hold value even when they are older?
faqs.a: An active rail spur is difficult to replicate on a new parcel given how built out the city already is, so tenants who ship by rail have few comparable buildings to choose from. That scarcity supports pricing even on older construction.

faqs.q: Should I order an environmental review before buying an older Commerce industrial building?
faqs.a: Yes. Decades of industrial and manufacturing use across the city mean prior tenants can leave soil or groundwater conditions that a walk-through will not reveal. A Phase I review ordered as soon as the property is identified protects the timeline as well as the underwriting.

faqs.q: Is Citadel Outlets-area retail underwritten the same way as Commerce industrial buildings?
faqs.a: No. A lender looking at retail near the Citadel corridor will weigh tenant sales performance more heavily than it would for a warehouse loan, where the building and rail access carry more of the underwriting.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Los Angeles confirm my Commerce property qualifies for an exchange?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates planning, property identification, and communication among an investor's advisors. Whether a specific transaction and property qualify is a determination made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
